current_legal_basis: Executive Order 13757 of December 28, 2016 (82 FR 1) took additional steps under the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 of April 1, 2015, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. That emergency was continued by a notice each year from 2017 through 2026; the held Notice of March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15511, FR Doc. 2026-06076) continues it for one year beyond April 1, 2026, and names Executive Order 13757, Executive Order 14144 and Executive Order 14306 among the orders that took additional steps under it. The held Federal Register texts of every executive order numbered 13758 through 14435 (14435 was signed 2026-10-05; orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are not held) do not revoke or supersede Executive Order 13757; the later amendments to the text it inserted are listed as later events. The Federal Register executive-order catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog, checked 2026-11-25) and the eCFR search (current-law:ecfr) show no revocation of the order. Checked through 2026-10-14.
reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 13757 restated section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694 to block property of the persons it describes (persons in the Annex, and persons the Secretary of the Treasury determines to have engaged in the described malicious cyber-enabled activities or related conduct). Executive Order 14144, section 9 (90 FR 6755, signed 2025-01-16, no deferred effective date stated), restated section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694 in full to read as follows. The restated text keeps the structure of paragraphs (i), (ii) and (iii) but changes the substance of the criteria (among other changes, it drops the word significant before threat in paragraph (ii), changes the purpose clause, and adds a ransomware criterion at (ii)(F)).
